mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome to a place where imagination, storytelling, and the magic of words come alive. Picture a world where the lines between reality and fantasy start to blur, and suddenly, the ordinary feels anything but. That’s the kind of journey we get to take together as we explore Neil Gaiman’s *The View from the Cheap Seats: Selected Nonfiction*. We’ll wander through libraries and comic conventions, and even the quiet, overlooked corners of everyday life. Along the way, Neil Gaiman invites us to reflect on the role that stories play in shaping who we are, why art and creativity matter, and how culture, myth, and memory weave together to create something unforgettable. Through his essays, speeches, and those thoughtful moments only he can craft, we’ll discover how literature, comics, music, and personal experience all unfold into a landscape filled with wonder. Stories, as Neil reminds us, act like mirrors and windows—sometimes showing us our deepest truths, and sometimes giving us a peek into worlds we’ve only dreamed about. So, let’s embark on this adventure with curiosity and a sense of reverence. We’ll celebrate the simple act of reading and writing, and see how it connects us, turning the mundane into something truly magical. Neil Gaiman’s warmth and wit will gently guide us toward a deeper appreciation for the stories that shape our identity and our communities. Together, we’ll discover why stories matter so much—and why, long after we finish the last page, they still linger with us.
